kept.q: Which tissue is mainly responsible for transporting water and dissolved mineral salts from the root to the leaves in a flowering plant such as maize?
kept.explanation: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes that carry water and mineral salts upward from the root to other parts of the plant. Phloem instead transports manufactured food like sugars. The cambium and cortex are not transport tissues.
kept.pidgin: Xylem na the tube wey dey carry water and mineral salt from root go leaf. Phloem na for food transport, e no be water. Cambium and cortex no be transport tissue at all.

kept.q: In human beings, which blood component is mainly responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues?
kept.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues. Plasma carries dissolved substances but not oxygen in large amounts. Platelets help in clotting, while white blood cells fight infection.
kept.pidgin: Red blood cells get haemoglobin wey dey hold oxygen from lungs go the body tissues. Plasma na liquid wey carry other substances, e no be oxygen carrier. Platelets na for clotting, white blood cells na for fight sickness.

kept.q: A student places a potted plant in the school garden under bright sun with a gentle breeze blowing. Which combination of conditions below would most likely increase the rate of transpiration in this plant?
options: Low light intensity and still air
kept.explanation: High temperature increases the kinetic energy of water molecules, making them evaporate faster from the leaf surface, while strong wind blows away the water vapour quickly, keeping the air around the leaf dry and increasing the rate of water loss. The other options describe cool, humid or still conditions which slow down transpiration.
kept.pidgin: When temperature high, water for leaf go evaporate faster, and when wind strong, e go carry the water vapour commot quick quick, so transpiration go dey fast. The other options na cool or wet condition wey go slow transpiration down.

kept.q: In the human circulatory system, which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood coming directly from the lungs?
kept.explanation: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium. The right atrium and right ventricle deal with deoxygenated blood from the body, while the left ventricle receives blood from the left atrium before pumping it to the body.
kept.pidgin: Pulmonary vein dey carry oxygen-rich blood from lungs enter left atrium. Right atrium and right ventricle dey handle blood wey never get oxygen, while left ventricle na im dey collect from left atrium before e pump am comot go body.

kept.q: A student cut a leafy twig and placed the cut end in a beaker of water containing red eosin dye, then kept the setup in bright sunlight. After two hours, the dye had risen noticeably up the stem into the leaf veins. Which of the following best explains the main force responsible for this upward movement, given that the twig has no roots?
options: Active transport by companion cells pushing the dye upward
Root pressure generated by osmotic absorption of water
Transpiration pull created by water loss from the leaf surface
Capillary action alone within the xylem vessels
kept.explanation: Since the twig has been cut and has no roots, root pressure cannot be responsible for the movement. As water evaporates from the leaf surface (transpiration), it creates a pulling force (tension) that draws water and the dissolved dye upward through the continuous xylem column, a process called transpiration pull.
kept.pidgin: Because dem don cut the twig and e no get root again, root pressure no fit be the reason. Na transpiration (water wey dey comot from leaf) dey create pulling force wey dey drag water and the dye go up inside the xylem, dem dey call am transpiration pull.

kept.q: Fish rely on a single circulatory system in which blood passes through the heart once for every complete circuit of the body, while mammals use a double circulatory system in which blood passes through the heart twice. What is the main advantage of the double circulatory system over the single one in terms of efficient transport of oxygen to body tissues?
options: It allows blood to be re-pressurised at the heart after passing through the lungs, maintaining higher blood pressure for efficient delivery to body tissues
It reduces the total number of blood vessels needed in the body
It allows blood to bypass the lungs completely whenever the animal is resting
It removes the need for a muscular heart in large, active animals
kept.explanation: In single circulation, blood loses pressure as it passes through the lung capillaries before reaching the body, making delivery slower. In double circulation, blood returns to the heart after the lungs and is pumped again at higher pressure to the body, allowing faster and more efficient oxygen supply to tissues, which suits active animals like mammals.
kept.pidgin: For single circulation, blood go lose pressure as e pass through lung capillaries before e reach body, so delivery go slow. For double circulation, blood go first return go heart after lungs, dem go pump am again with more pressure go body, so oxygen go reach tissue fast well well, dis one good pass for active animals like mammal.
